# ERRORS.md — the ERROR-SURFACE TABLE

Every distinct way the C reference implementation (libpng 1.6.59, built with
`c_src/include/pnglibconf.h`) rejects or errors on input.  Derived mechanically
from the C sources: one row per `png_error` / `png_chunk_error` /
`png_app_error` / `png_benign_error` / `png_chunk_benign_error` / `png_warning`
/ `png_chunk_warning` / `png_app_warning` / `png_chunk_report` /
`png_fixed_error` call site, per `return NULL` / `return 0` / `return -1` /
`return handled_error` failure sentinel, per explicit range / null / limit
check, and per min/max constant.

## Build-configuration facts that determine the observable result

* `PNG_BENIGN_WRITE_ERRORS_SUPPORTED` is **OFF** (`pnglibconf.h:24`);
  `PNG_BENIGN_ERRORS_SUPPORTED` and `PNG_BENIGN_READ_ERRORS_SUPPORTED` are ON.
* `PNG_LIBPNG_BUILD_BASE_TYPE == PNG_LIBPNG_BUILD_BETA` (2) `<`
  `PNG_LIBPNG_BUILD_RC` (3), so `PNG_RELEASE_BUILD == 0`.  Therefore
  `PNG_FLAG_APP_ERRORS_WARN` / `PNG_FLAG_APP_WARNINGS_WARN` are never set by
  default and **`png_app_error` and `png_app_warning` are both fatal
  `png_error`s** unless `png_set_benign_errors(png_ptr, 1)` was called.
* `png_benign_error` → warning on a *read* struct, fatal on a *write* struct.
* `png_chunk_report(..., PNG_CHUNK_WRITE_ERROR)` → non-fatal on read, fatal on
  write (`pngerror.c:486-512`).
* `PNG_FIXED_POINT_MACRO_SUPPORTED` is OFF, so `png_fixed` / `png_fixed_ITU`
  are real functions that can raise `"fixed point overflow in <text>"`.
* Limits in force: `PNG_USER_WIDTH_MAX` = `PNG_USER_HEIGHT_MAX` = 1000000,
  `PNG_USER_CHUNK_MALLOC_MAX` = 8000000, `PNG_USER_CHUNK_CACHE_MAX` = 1000,
  `PNG_MAX_GAMMA_8` = 11, `PNG_GAMMA_THRESHOLD_FIXED` = 5000,
  `PNG_WARNING_PARAMETER_COUNT` = 8, `PNG_MAX_ERROR_TEXT` = 196.

## How the rows are tested

Rows are covered by the differential error-path tests in `tests/`
(`t20_err_*.rs`, `t21_err_*.rs`, ...).  Because `png_error` must not return,
the low-level rows are exercised in a **sub-process**: the test binary
re-executes itself once per library with an error handler that prints the
message and exits, and the parent asserts the two transcripts (warnings, in
order, then the error message, then the exit code) are byte-identical.  Rows
reachable through the simplified API are additionally checked in-process by
comparing `png_image.warning_or_error` and `png_image.message`.

Rows flagged **not compiled in this build** are `#ifdef`-excluded here and are
therefore not reachable; they are retained for completeness of the surface.

## Coverage summary

| | count |
|---|---|
| rows total | 1183 |
| rows with a passing differential error-path test | 1131 |
| rows `n/a` — `#ifdef`-excluded from this configuration, or a documented spot where the C has NO check (so the input is undefined behaviour, not a rejection) | 52 |

The `covered by` column names the test file(s) that construct that exact
invalid input, call BOTH libraries and assert the SAME rejection.  Two
mechanisms are used:

* **in-process**, when the rejection returns a sentinel or is caught by
  `png_safe_execute` (the whole simplified API), so the exact
  `warning_or_error` code and the exact message string can be compared;
* **sub-process**, when the rejection is a `png_error` that must not return —
  the test binary re-executes itself once per library with a handler that prints
  the message and exits, and the parent compares the whole transcript
  (every warning, in order, then the error text, then the exit status and the
  terminating signal).

Every test file that uses the sub-process mechanism also contains a
`self_check` / `subprocess_self_check` test asserting that the C library really
does emit the expected distinct messages, so a comparison can never pass
vacuously by comparing nothing.

### Inputs deliberately NOT tested (C-level undefined behaviour, no check exists)

These were each attempted, found to segfault or abort in BOTH libraries with no
diagnostic, verified against the C source to have no guard, and are recorded
here instead of being asserted:

| function | input | why untestable |
|---|---|---|
| `png_sig_cmp` | `sig == NULL` with `num_to_check >= 1` | reaches `memcmp(&sig[start], ...)` (png.c:96) |
| `png_convert_to_rfc1123_buffer` | `ptime == NULL` | dereferences `ptime->year` (png.c:751) |
| `png_write_image` | `image == NULL` | dereferences `image[i]` |
| `png_write_row` | `row == NULL` | no NULL check |
| `png_write_data` | never calling `png_set_write_fn` | `png_default_write_data` calls `fwrite` on a NULL `FILE*`; and passing NULL to `png_set_write_fn` installs that same default (pngwio.c:130), so the "Call to NULL write function" branch (pngwio.c:40) is unreachable through the public API |
| `png_image_begin_read_from_memory` | non-NULL but bogus `image->opaque` | `png_image_read_init` only allocates when `opaque == NULL` (pngread.c:1130), then the caller dereferences `image->opaque->memory` (pngread.c:1448) |
| `png_free_data` | `num` outside the stored array | indexes `info_ptr->text[num]` with no bounds check (png.c:498) |
| `png_get_io_state`, `png_get_io_chunk_type` | `png_ptr == NULL` | no NULL guard (pngget.c:1344, 1350) |
| `png_set_benign_errors`, `png_set_check_for_invalid_index` | `png_ptr == NULL` | no NULL guard (pngset.c:1926, 1956) |
| `png_set_read_user_transform_fn` | `png_ptr == NULL` | no NULL guard (pngrtran.c:1133) |
| `png_get_eXIf_1`, `png_get_PLTE`, `png_get_sCAL*` | individual out-parameters NULL while the chunk IS present | written to unconditionally (pngget.c:910, 1140, 1042-1087) |
| `png_do_read_interlace` | a user transform declaring `depth * channels > 64` bits on an INTERLACED image (`png_set_user_transform_info(png_ptr, NULL, 32, 4)`) | the routine copies through a `png_byte v[8]` whose own comment asserts `/* SAFE; pixel_depth does not exceed 64 */` (pngrutil.c:3927); the C overruns that stack buffer and merely survives by luck. The Rust translation faults instead. Non-interlaced `> 64`-bit user transforms agree in both libraries and ARE covered. |
| `png_set_quantize` | `num_palette < 0` or `> 256`; `maximum_colors <= 0` with `histogram == NULL` | `memcpy` into the fixed 256-entry `png_ptr->palette` (pngrtran.c:823) and `hash[i]` indexed past its 769 entries (pngrtran.c:725) |
| `png_set_keep_unknown_chunks` | a `chunk_list` shorter than `5 * num_chunks` | `chunk_list + 5*i` read unchecked (pngset.c:1719) |
| `png_fixed`, `png_fixed_ITU` | `NaN` | the range test at png.c:2737 / png.c:2756 does not fire for NaN and the following cast to `png_fixed_point` / `png_uint_32` is UB (x86 `cvttsd2si` yields `INT_MIN`, Rust's `as` saturates — a difference in UB, not in defined behaviour) |
| `png_default_read_data`, `png_default_write_data` | `io_ptr == NULL` | `fread` / `fwrite` called on it with no check (pngrio.c:59, pngwio.c:57); a real stdio stream is used in the tests instead |
| `png_benign_error`, `png_chunk_benign_error` | `png_ptr == NULL` | dereference `png_ptr->flags` with no check (pngerror.c:310, pngerror.c:463) |

### Rows that are present in the C but UNREACHABLE for any input

Verified against the source rather than asserted:

| row | why unreachable |
|---|---|
| `png_check_IHDR` "Image width is too large for this architecture" (png.c:1989) | the threshold derives from `PNG_SIZE_MAX`; on 64-bit it is ~`0x1fff_ffff_ffff_fffd`, above every `png_uint_32`. The C comment itself says the comparison "will always be false" on 64-bit systems. |
| `png_zalloc` "Potential overflow in png_zalloc()" (png.c:118) | the test is `items >= (~(png_alloc_size_t)0) / size`; with both operands `unsigned int` the smallest right-hand side is `(2^64-1)/(2^32-1) = 2^32+1`, larger than any 32-bit `items`. The C comment calls the check "vestigial". |
| `png_malloc_base` `size > PNG_SIZE_MAX` (pngmem.c:88) | `PNG_SIZE_MAX == SIZE_MAX` and `size` is a `size_t`, so the test is dead. The reachable overflow guard is `png_malloc_array_checked` (pngmem.c:113), which IS covered. |
| `png_read_data` / `png_write_data` "Call to NULL read/write function" (pngrio.c:95, pngwio.c:130) | passing NULL to `png_set_read_fn` / `png_set_write_fn` installs the stdio default instead, so the NULL branch cannot be reached. The cross-wiring warnings (pngrio.c:106, pngwio.c:157) ARE reachable and are covered, including the shared message text. |
| `pngrutil.c:824` (the only `zstream.msg` report that does not go through zlib) | `png_read_buffer`'s limit at pngrutil.c:380 is strictly larger and rejects the chunk first. |

### `png_zstream_error`: only 3 of its 10 messages are observable

Every code path that ends in `png_error(png_ptr, png_ptr->zstream.msg)` first calls
`deflateInit2` / `deflateReset` / `inflateInit2` / `inflateReset2`, and zlib
assigns `strm->msg = Z_NULL` inside each of those before validating — so a string
placed in `zstream.msg` by `png_zstream_error` cannot be read back out through any
public entry point.  `t24_err_misc.rs` therefore (a) calls `png_zstream_error`
directly with all nine zlib return codes plus six out-of-range codes, on read and
write structs, asserting both libraries stay silent and the struct remains usable,
and (b) drives real corrupt zlib streams.  Three messages are reachable that way
and all three are asserted verbatim: `"missing LZ dictionary"` (FDICT set),
`"truncated"` (`Z_BUF_ERROR`), `"bad parameters to zlib"` (write-side
`deflateInit2` failure).  `"zlib IO error"` (`Z_ERRNO`, only produced by zlib's
gz* API, which libpng never calls) and `"unsupported zlib version"`
(`Z_VERSION_ERROR`) cannot be produced by any input to this library.

Two rows resolve to `PNG_ABORT()` rather than a message and are compared as
such (identical terminating signal in both libraries): `png_longjmp` with no
`jmp_buf` installed, and `png_error` with `png_ptr == NULL`.

| # | function | trigger (the exact invalid input/condition) | expected C result | covered by |
|---|----------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------|-----------|

| 1 | `png_error` (`pngerror.c:39`) | called with any `error_message`; `png_ptr != NULL && png_ptr->error_fn != NULL` | calls `(*error_fn)(png_ptr, error_message)`; if it returns, falls through to `png_default_error` -> `png_longjmp(png_ptr, 1)` -> non-zero `setjmp`; declared `PNG_NORETURN` | t23_err_write.rs, t24_err_misc.rs |
| 2 | `png_error` (`pngerror.c:42`) | `png_ptr == NULL` or `png_ptr->error_fn == NULL` | skips custom handler, calls `png_default_error(png_ptr, error_message)` -> `png_longjmp(png_ptr,1)`; never returns | t23_err_write.rs, t24_err_misc.rs |
